module_name: Discounted Cash Flow (DCF) and Growth Models

quiz.name: 2027 Equities - Module 6 Discounted Cash Flow (DCF) and Growth Models

entry.title: 2027 Equities Mod6-Q1
entry.itemBody: Which of the following statements best describes the difference between the FCFE (free cash flow to equity) metric and dividends?

choices.itemBody: A. FCFE involves cash flows to shareholders in the form of both share buybacks and cash dividends.
B. FCFE includes dividends, retained earnings, and changes in cash.

C. FCFE includes changes in cash plus dividends minus changes in equity. Feedback C is correct because it incorporates net cash flows distributed and available to shareholders once other obligations are satisfied. B is incorrect because it ignores changes in equity from new issuance and share buybacks. A is incorrect because it omits cash available to shareholders

entry.title: 2027 Equities Mod6-Q2
entry.itemBody: Which of the following statements best describes the relationship between FCFE and FCFF?

choices.itemBody: A. FCFF and FCFE are equal as long as debt outstanding does not change.
B. When debt financing is used, a firm’s FCFF will exceed FCFE as long as debt outstanding remains unchanged.

C. FCFF is always either greater than or equal to FCFE. Feedback B is correct because FCFF is equal to FCFE plus after-tax interest expense less debt changes. C is incorrect because FCFF can fall below FCFE if debt outstanding changes. A is incorrect because FCFF and FCFE cannot be equal if debt is outstanding; they can be equal only if no debt is used by the firm.

entry.title: 2027 Equities Mod6-Q5
entry.itemBody: Which of the following statements best explains why preferred shares have a lower required rate of return than common shares for a given issuer?

choices.itemBody: A. Preferred shareholders have a priority claim over common stock in the receipt of dividends and on the issuer’s assets in the event of liquidation.
B. Preferred shareholders receive fixed dividends, while common shares receive discretionary dividends.

C. Preferred shares generally have contingency features that represent an economic benefit to the issuer, resulting in a lower expected return. Feedback A is correct because the priority claim over common stock in the receipt of dividends and on assets under liquidation is the primary driver of the lower expected rate of return. B is incorrect because the type or size of the dividend does not affect the discount rate applied based on the required rate of return. C is incorrect because contingency features associated with preferred shares may represent an economic benefit to either an issuer or an investor.
